evals.prompt: Write the FRD for the 'Expense Approval Flow' of Ledgerly, our SMB expense-management SaaS. The approved PRD (v1.2) defines: PRD-001 (Must) employees submit an expense with receipt photo and category, Trace: BR-001; PRD-002 (Must) manager approves or rejects with a reason, and approvals over 1,000 EUR require a second approver from finance, Trace: BR-001; PRD-003 (Should) submitter is notified of the decision, Trace: BR-002. Actors: Employee, Manager, Finance Approver. Known constraints from product: max receipt upload 10 MB; decisions must be notified quickly (product wants 'within minutes'). Cover the behavior in full, including what happens when things go wrong (approver leaves the company mid-flow, duplicate submission, oversized upload, rejected-then-resubmitted expense).
evals.expected_output: A complete FRD with document control tracing to PRD v1.2, actors, atomic 'The system shall...' functional requirements each carrying an immortal FR-NNN ID with a 'Trace: PRD-NNN' line, declarative Given/When/Then acceptance criteria suffixed [FR-NNN] (one behavior per scenario, paste-ready for story cards), an explicit Error & Edge States section covering the listed failure cases, fit-criterion NFRs (percentile + threshold + window + load condition + breach consequence) for notification latency, and two-way traceability — with no implementation design.
expectations: Output includes Document Control declaring upward trace to the PRD, plus an Actors section covering Employee, Manager, and Finance Approver
Every functional requirement carries an immortal FR-NNN ID and a 'Trace: PRD-001/002/003' line to the supplied PRD IDs — no orphan FRs, no dotted sub-IDs like FR-002.1

Requirements use 'The system shall...' statements and are atomic — the two-tier approval rule (over 1,000 EUR needs a finance second approver) is its own requirement, not fused into the general approve/reject requirement
Acceptance criteria are written as Given/When/Then blocks, each suffixed with its [FR-NNN] tag so they paste unchanged into a story card's Scenarios section
Gherkin is declarative business intent (e.g. 'Given a submitted expense over 1,000 EUR'), never UI clicks or internals (no button names, no service/JWT/API internals)
Each scenario covers exactly one behavior (1:1 scenario-to-acceptance-criterion), including at least one rejection-path scenario, not only happy paths
An explicit Error & Edge States section exists and addresses the prompt's failure cases: approver departure mid-flow, duplicate submission, oversized (>10 MB) upload, and resubmission after rejection

The 'within minutes' notification ask is turned into a fit-criterion NFR with an NFR-NNN ID stating percentile + threshold + measurement window + load condition + breach consequence, not a bare 'P95 <= X' figure
A Traceability section links up to PRD IDs and down to stories/tests, and the FRD contains no implementation design (no database, framework, or vendor choices)

evals.prompt: The team lead pinged me: 'We're revamping notifications across the app. Can you get the functional spec written today?' There is no PRD for this revamp, I don't know which user roles are affected, nobody has listed which notification types are in scope, and there are no designs or acceptance expectations yet. Write the FSD.
evals.expected_output: A response that does not fabricate a full FSD: it names the skill's missing required inputs (product scope, personas/actors, features and edge cases in scope, acceptance expectations and relevant NFRs, designs/story references), asks targeted questions or produces a clearly gap-marked skeleton, refuses to invent behaviors or upstream PRD-NNN parents (using 'Trace: derived' only for genuinely engineering-imposed items rather than fake parents), and insists that error/edge states and testable acceptance criteria cannot be filled in without the missing inputs.
expectations: The response flags missing required inputs by name, covering at least: upstream product scope/PRD, actors or user roles, features/workflows and edge cases in scope, and acceptance expectations or relevant NFRs

The response asks concrete clarifying questions (which notification types, which roles, what triggers, what does done look like) or marks explicit gaps — it does not deliver a complete-looking spec built on invented behavior

No fake upstream traceability: the response does not mint 'Trace: PRD-NNN' lines to a PRD that does not exist — it either flags the missing PRD or notes that requirements without a business parent are marked 'Trace: derived', never given a fabricated parent
Any draft requirements offered are still atomic, uniquely FR-NNN-identified, and in 'The system shall...' form — the standard is not abandoned just because inputs are missing

The response flags that an Error & Edge States section is mandatory and cannot be completed without knowing the workflows — the section is not silently omitted or padded with invented cases presented as fact
The response does not silently invent numeric NFR targets — latency/delivery figures are requested or explicitly marked as placeholders needing an owner
The response keeps implementation design out of scope (no queueing/push-provider/architecture choices)
The response mentions validating traceability (which upstream need each requirement serves) before the spec can be approved

evals.prompt:
Review this excerpt of our draft FRD against your functional-spec standards. Itemize every defect you find and how to fix each:

# FRD — Password Reset
Status: draft

## Functional Requirements
- The system should be fast and easy to use.
- FR-010: The system shall send a reset email and log the user in automatically after reset and lock the account after repeated failures.
- FR-010.1: The reset link expires.
- Users can change their email address.

## Acceptance Criteria
  GIVEN the AuthService returns a valid reset token from Redis
  WHEN the user clicks the blue 'Reset now' button on the modal
  THEN the ResetController updates the password hash

## Non-Functional
- NFR-001: P95 <= 800ms.
evals.expected_output: A structured review that catches every planted defect: the untestable 'fast and easy to use' requirement, FR-010 bundling three behaviors into one non-atomic statement, the forbidden dotted sub-ID FR-010.1, the ID-less untraced 'users can change their email' requirement (also scope creep with no upstream parent), the imperative implementation-coupled Gherkin (Redis/AuthService/blue button/ResetController) that must be rewritten declaratively, the completely missing Error & Edge States section, and the template-fill NFR 'P95 <= 800ms' lacking window, load condition, and breach consequence — each tied to the skill's rules with a concrete rewrite.
expectations: The review flags 'The system should be fast and easy to use' as untestable and shows a measurable rewrite (the skill's anti-pattern: attach a numeric threshold such as a P95 target)
The review flags FR-010 as non-atomic — it bundles send-email, auto-login, and account-lockout — and requires splitting into separate FR-NNN statements that can be traced and tested independently
The review flags FR-010.1 as a forbidden dotted/positional sub-ID: IDs are immortal and flat, and a requirement needing children is not atomic

The review flags 'Users can change their email address' as lacking an FR-NNN ID, lacking a Trace line, and being an orphan/scope-creep requirement with no upstream parent (and off-topic for a password-reset spec)

The review flags the Gherkin as imperative and implementation-coupled — AuthService, Redis, ResetController, and the blue button are internals/UI clicks — and rewrites it as declarative business intent
The review notes the acceptance criteria carry no [FR-NNN] suffix tags, breaking the paste-through convention into story-card scenarios
The review flags the missing Error & Edge States section (expired link, reuse of a used link, unknown email, repeated requests) as a mandatory-section omission — the most common senior-review bounce
The review flags NFR-001 'P95 <= 800ms' as template-fill: a fit criterion needs percentile + threshold + measurement window + load condition + breach consequence, and a Trace line
Defects are itemized individually with concrete fixes, not summarized in one vague paragraph
